facts.text: Babbie was first settled in the 1830s, and by 1851 the community had built its first church, the Bethel Primitive Baptist Church.
In 1901 the Alabama and Florida Railroad laid tracks through Babbie, making it a flag stop on a line that became part of the Louisville and Nashville Railroad.
Early businesses in Babbie revolved around agriculture, featuring a grist mill, cotton gin, feed mill, and sawmill that served the farming community.
Local lore suggests the town’s name comes from a playful twist on “baby,” reflecting how small the settlement was when it began.
The town’s first school opened in the early 1900s, and a post office operated from 1902 until 1911, marking a brief period of expanded services.
Today, Babbie remains largely a farming community, preserving its rural character amid modern changes.
